about.title: About Home Affordability Calculator
about.description: The Home Affordability Calculator helps you determine how much house you can afford based on your income, expenses, and financial situation. This comprehensive tool considers your monthly income, existing debts, down payment, interest rates, and other factors to calculate your maximum home purchase price and monthly payment capacity. Whether you're a first-time homebuyer or looking to upgrade, this calculator provides realistic affordability estimates to guide your home buying decisions.

howTo.title: How to Use the Home Affordability Calculator

steps.title: Enter Income Information
steps.description: Input your gross monthly income from all sources including salary, bonuses, and other regular income.

steps.title: Add Monthly Debts
steps.description: Enter your existing monthly debt payments including credit cards, car loans, and student loans.

steps.title: Set Down Payment
steps.description: Specify your available down payment amount and preferred down payment percentage.

steps.title: Interest Rate
steps.description: Enter the current mortgage interest rate or use the default market rate.

steps.title: Additional Costs
steps.description: Include property taxes, insurance, and HOA fees for comprehensive affordability analysis.

steps.title: Review Affordability Results
steps.description: Analyze your maximum home price, monthly payment, and debt-to-income ratios.

tips: Keep total housing costs under 28% of gross monthly income
Maintain total debt payments under 36% of gross monthly income
Save for closing costs (2-5% of home price) beyond down payment

faq.q: How much house can I afford with my income?
faq.a: Generally, you can afford a home that costs 2.5-3 times your annual income, with monthly housing costs not exceeding 28% of gross monthly income. For example, with a $75,000 annual income, you might afford a $200,000-$225,000 home.

faq.q: What is the 28/36 rule for home affordability?
faq.a: The 28/36 rule states that housing costs shouldn't exceed 28% of gross monthly income, and total debt payments shouldn't exceed 36%. This helps ensure you can comfortably afford mortgage payments while maintaining financial stability.

faq.q: How does my down payment affect affordability?
faq.a: Larger down payments increase affordability by reducing loan amount and eliminating PMI (if 20% or more). A 20% down payment on a $300,000 home saves about $200-300 monthly compared to 5% down.

faq.q: Should I get pre-approved before house hunting?
faq.a: Yes, pre-approval gives you a realistic budget, shows sellers you're serious, and can speed up the buying process. However, don't feel obligated to spend the maximum amount you're approved for.
